fields: IAM's name
Met-A distance to ceiling (instrument 12b, distance to maximum disorder).
In the field's terms
Headroom: distance from maximum methylation entropy for the whole-sample reading.
Definition
How far the whole-sample Met-A sits from the most disordered state its own cells can reach.
What it does
It says how much of the way to complete disorder the sample has gone, for whole-sample Met-A.
Why the instrument needs it
A Met-A move means more when it is placed against the ceiling the sample's own cells can reach at its read depth.
How it is obtained or computed
(A_sat - A) / (A_sat - 1), with the saturation level A_sat counted at the sample's own read depth.
Where it is read
Every atlas site, through the whole-sample Met-A.
Where IAM's Law enters

IAM's Law, link 3 (the half and the ceiling), long form section 3, 'Step 3: the virial half'. The packet carries only that section's title, so what the step says and its status are open: not in the records yet.
Long-form section
link 3: long form section 3
Healthy value and how it is set
Output: healthy is about 1 when healthy. The development test reads 1.18476: reading 1.185 because Met-A reads 0.894 (the offset); OK otherwise.
Where its value comes from
computed by the chain from the sample's molecules and its references
Its setting on IAM's Law Sphere
a reading, not a setting (the lever map shows which settings move it)
Lever range (what moves, by how much)
open: not written yet
Limits and what is open
It inherits Met-A's offset: while Met-A reads 0.894 the distance reads 1.185. It places the reading on a scale, not a cause.

Headroom: distance from maximum methylation entropy at CpG islands.

How far the CpG-island reading sits from the most disordered state the sample's own cells can reach.

fields: How it works

Headroom = (A_sat - A) / (A_sat - 1), where A is Met-A (or the islands reading) and A_sat the value complete disorder would give, counted at the sample's own read depth: 1 = at the healthy floor, 0 = completely disordered.
Why
Met-A says how much disorder rose; the headroom says how much of the way to complete disorder the sample has gone, which counting depth would otherwise distort.
Physics
IAM's Law, link 3 (the half and the ceiling): the gauge's ends are derived, the floor a perfectly held record, the ceiling complete disorder.
Where the data comes from
Met-A's and the islands' readings and expectation; the sample's read counts.
The numbers
Test library GSM5652214: 1.185, because Met-A read 0.894 there before the tare; it moves with Met-A.
Method and standard
Counted saturation at the sample's own depth; its bar follows Met-A's (owed).
Known-answer test
Follows Met-A's known answer (owed after a chain update).
Limits
(1) Depends entirely on Met-A's expectation. (2) Not yet commissioned against samples with known departures.
Where the result goes
bundle met_a_whole.ceiling and the islands ceiling; report.
Code
stage_metaa_atlas (ceiling)
How to rebuild it
1. Compute Met-A and A_sat at the sample's read counts. 2. (A_sat - A) / (A_sat - 1).
History
Dated entries in the development log (METHYLPHYS_DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md) and the instrument's development record.
